rules.problem: Korea has STRICT garbage rules. Using wrong bags = fines up to 100,000 won.
action: Buy 종량제 봉투 (official waste bags) at any convenience store — 5L/10L/20L sizes
Food waste (음식물 쓰레기) goes in SEPARATE green bins
Recycling: separate into glass/plastic/paper/cans
Never leave garbage out on wrong day — check your building's schedule
Large items (furniture): contact 주민센터 for special collection

rules.problem: The ARC (외국인등록증) is MANDATORY if staying over 90 days. Missing the deadline = legal violation and fines.
action: Apply within 90 days of arrival at 출입국관리소 (immigration office)
Book appointment at HiKorea.go.kr FIRST — walk-ins usually not accepted
Bring: passport, university enrollment certificate, 2 passport photos, 30,000 won
ARC needed for: bank account, proper phone plan, renting, health insurance
Processing takes 2-4 weeks — apply early!

rules.problem: Opening a Korean bank account requires some preparation but it's straightforward.
action: Easiest: Kakao Bank (mobile only) — open with Korean phone number + passport
Best for foreigners: Shinhan (신한) or KB Kookmin (국민)
Need: ARC + passport (or passport + enrollment cert for new arrivals at some banks)
Cheapest international transfer: Wise app > bank wire
Campus bank branch is usually most foreigner-friendly

rules.problem: You need a Korean phone number for banking, government apps, and daily life.
action: Airport: buy at SK Telecom, KT, or LG U+ booth in arrivals area
Full plan needs ARC — start with prepaid SIM if you just arrived
Student plans: ~20,000-30,000 won/month for unlimited calls + 10GB+ data
Budget option: 알뜰폰 (MVNO) plans from HelloMobile, LycaMobile

rules.problem: 층간소음 (floor noise) is taken very seriously in Korea. Can cause lease problems.
action: Quiet hours: 10PM-7AM
Wear slippers indoors — reduces noise significantly
If you get complaint: apologize immediately and fix it
Your neighbor noisy? Call 층간소음이웃사이센터 at 1661-2642

rules.problem: Adjusting to a new country is genuinely hard. Feeling lonely or overwhelmed is completely normal.
action: University 학생상담센터 (counseling center): FREE and confidential, often has English
Foreigner helpline: 1345 (24/7, multilingual)
Join international student groups on Facebook/KakaoTalk
Give yourself time — most students say months 2-3 are hardest. It gets better.
If feelings last more than 2 weeks: please speak with a counselor

rules.problem: Emergency situation detected. Here are Korea's emergency numbers.
action: 🚨 Police: 112 (24/7) — say 'English please' for interpreter
🚑 Ambulance/Fire: 119 (24/7) — say 'English please'
🌐 Foreigner helpline: 1345 (24/7, many languages)
In text: just type 112 and location if you can't speak
Nearest hospital: search 응급실 on Naver Maps

rules.problem: Korean public transport is excellent but requires a transit card.
action: T-Money card (티머니): 4,000 won at CU/GS25/7-Eleven, charge at station or store
Subway: 1,250-1,550 won per ride based on distance
Bus: ~1,200 won, free transfer within 30 minutes on T-Money
Apps: Kakao Maps for bus routes, Naver Maps for walking + subway
Last subway: approximately 11:30PM-midnight depending on line

rules.problem: Healthcare is affordable with insurance but expensive without. Make sure you understand your status.
action: NHIS (국민건강보험): auto-enrolled after 6 months stay, ~30,000-40,000/month
With NHIS: pay only 20-30% of hospital costs
University clinic: cheapest option for minor illness
Pharmacy (약국): no prescription needed for basic medicine
Emergency: 119 or search 응급실 on Naver Maps

rules.problem: International students are frequently targeted by scams in Korea.
action: Voice phishing (보이스피싱): Korean government NEVER asks for money over phone. Hang up.
Fake jobs offering unusually high pay for easy work = scam
Rental fraud: always check 등기부등본 before paying any deposit
Report scams: ecrm.police.go.kr or call 182
Advice: 1345 helpline (English available)

rules.problem: International students have specific work hour limits. Exceeding them = visa violation.
action: D-2 visa: max 25 hours/week during semester, unlimited during vacation
D-4 visa: need separate work permit (시간제취업허가) from immigration
Apply for work permit at HiKorea.go.kr before starting any job
Popular student jobs: cafe, restaurant, convenience store, tutoring, translation
Min wage 2025: ~9,860 won/hour (check current rate at labour.go.kr)
